newsitem.title: FRANCE: No rain expected in France, drought fears gain.
newsitem.headline: No rain expected in France, drought fears gain.

text.p: French weather forecasters offered more bad news on Friday to farmers already suffering a three-month dry spell with predictions of at least another five days without rain.

The lack of rain combined with mild temperatures has raised fears of drought among farmers, pushed the government to impose partial irrigation bans in some places and boosted the price of French grain on international markets.

France's breadbasket Beauce region has received only 90 millimetres (three inches) of rain this year, about the normal. In the southwest around Bordeaux, a mere 80 millimetres of rain has fallen, 30 percent of the usual.
Weather forecasters, government officials and farming experts, while worried by the lack of rain, are refusing to forecast a full blown drought.
"The situation is worrying, but not irreversible," an Agriculture Ministry official told Reuters. He said rain in the next two weeks would avert serious economic damage.

"Last year we had the same exact set of circumstances at the same time," said Benedicte Cailler, spokeswoman at the AGPB wheat growers association. "Then the situation reversed itself and we had a good harvest."
"It's not a catastrophe," one farmer in the Beauce told the daily Le Monde. "The surface of the fields are dry because of the wind. Underneath it's still wet, but it's time for it to rain."

The office of the government representative in the Nord Pas-de-Calais region called on residents to restrict water use. The largest farm union said on Thursday it had set up a crisis team to monitor crop conditions across the country.
Spring vegetables and fruits such as asparagus and strawberries have been available in stores weeks ahead of expectations this year.

Cherries are ripening between two weeks and a month early, said Patrick Galois, a forecaster at the national weather service Meteo France. Farmers have complained of price competition with Spanish produce that is usually in stores about a month ahead of French equivalents.
